verses.commentary: Micah of Moresheth (a village near Gath) prophesied during three kings: Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah. Contemporary with Isaiah in Judah and Hosea in Israel. His vision concerns both Samaria and Jerusalem. The entire divided kingdom stands under scrutiny.

Universal summons: all peoples, the earth and its inhabitants. Creation itself is called to witness. The Sovereign Lord testifies against his people from his holy temple. The courtroom spans the cosmos.
Theophany: the Lord comes from his dwelling place, treads on earth's heights. Divine descent. God leaves his sanctuary to judge. The heights (mountains, places of pride) become footstools.
Mountains melt, valleys split. Wax before fire, water rushing downhill. Natural phenomena describe supernatural intervention. What seems solid liquefies under divine presence.

All this because of Jacob's transgression. What is Jacob's transgression? Samaria. What is Judah's high place? Jerusalem. Capital cities embody national sin. Where power concentrates, corruption concentrates.
Samaria becomes rubble, a place for vineyards. Stones poured into the valley, foundations exposed. Urban devastation. The city returns to agriculture. What was built is unbuilt.

Idols broken, temple gifts burned, images destroyed. What was gathered from prostitute wages returns to prostitute wages. Ill gotten gain cycles back to original purpose. Corruption produces corruption.
The prophet's personal response: weeping, wailing, going barefoot and naked, howling like a jackal, moaning like an owl. Micah embodies lament. Proclamation through passionate grief.
Samaria's wound is incurable. The plague has spread to Judah, reached Jerusalem's gate. Infection crossing borders. What destroyed the north threatens the south. Sin is contagious.
Tell it not in Gath (the Philistine city). Weep not at all. In Beth Ophrah (House of Dust) roll in dust. Wordplay on city names begins. Each town's name becomes its fate.

Shaphir (Beautiful) passes by naked and shamed. Zaanan (Going Out) does not come out. Beth Ezel (House of Support) mourns, offers no support. Each name inverted. Beauty becomes shame, going becomes staying, support fails.
Maroth (Bitterness) writhes waiting for relief. Disaster from the Lord reaches Jerusalem's gate. The capital is not exempt. Divine judgment moves systematically toward the center.
Lachish (Horse City) told to harness horses. Here the sin of Daughter Zion began. Transgressions of Israel found there. Lachish as conduit of corruption from north to south.
Parting gifts to Moresheth Gath (Possession of Gath). Akzib (Deception) proves deceptive. Towns given away like dowry. What was possessed is dispossessed. Names become fates.
A conqueror against Mareshah (Possession). Nobles flee to Adullam (David's cave refuge). The powerful hide where David once hid. Royalty reduced to fugitives.
Shave your head for your delightful children. Make yourself bald as a vulture. They go into exile. Mourning ritual for living children. Exile is death to the parents who remain.
